package_info.package_manager: npm (also PyPI, RubyGems, JCenter, Bintray, Maven Central discussed)
package_info.package_versions: All versions of attacker-uploaded packages with names matching internal/private dependencies
package_info.why_malicious: These packages are intentionally published to public repositories with names that exactly match internal or private dependencies used by target organizations. When build systems or dependency resolvers encounter these names, they may inadvertently fetch and install the attacker's package instead of the intended internal one, resulting in arbitrary code execution and potential supply chain compromise.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code reads the /etc/passwd file and sends its contents via HTTP POST to a hardcoded attacker-controlled domain, resulting in exfiltration of sensitive system data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Postinstall scripts that access sensitive files and transmit their contents to external servers are highly indicative of malicious activity, as legitimate packages rarely require such actions during installation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages should not access or exfiltrate sensitive files, nor should they make unsolicited network requests during installation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may use postinstall scripts for setup or telemetry, but they do not access or transmit sensitive files such as /etc/passwd.
key_indicators: Network requests initiated from postinstall scripts
Access to sensitive files (e.g., /etc/passwd, environment variables) during installation
Hardcoded external domains in installation scripts

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code accesses the SECRET_TOKEN environment variable and sends its value to a hardcoded domain via HTTPS POST, enabling credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Import-time code that accesses environment variables and immediately exfiltrates their values to an external server is a clear sign of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not perform network exfiltration or access secrets from environment variables during import.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, some packages may perform telemetry or error reporting at import, but they do not transmit sensitive environment variables.
key_indicators: Access to environment variables at import-time
Network requests to hardcoded external endpoints during import
Immediate exfiltration of sensitive data upon package import

attack_chain.action: Attacker identifies internal or private package names used by target organizations.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker publishes malicious packages with matching names to public repositories.

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes malicious packages with high version numbers to public repositories (npm, PyPI, etc).
attack_chain.leads_to: Build systems resolve dependencies and may fetch the attacker's package instead of the internal one.

attack_chain.action: Build systems or developer environments install the malicious package.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes during installation or import-time.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes, exfiltrating sensitive files or environment variables to attacker-controlled domains.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to secrets, credentials, or sensitive data from the target environment.

behavioral_signatures: postinstall or import-time scripts making network requests to external domains
Access to sensitive files (e.g., /etc/passwd) or environment variables during installation or import
Package names in public repositories that exactly match known internal or private dependencies
file_indicators: package.json with suspicious postinstall scripts containing network or file access commands
setup.py or __init__.py with code that performs network exfiltration
index.js with HTTP requests to hardcoded, unknown domains
network_indicators: HTTP/HTTPS requests to attacker-controlled or unknown domains (e.g., https://attacker.com/exfil) during install or import
Unusual outbound connections from build, CI/CD, or developer environments at install/import time
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor public repositories for packages with names matching internal dependencies. Flag postinstall or import-time scripts that access sensitive files or environment variables and make network requests. Alert on outbound connections to unknown or untrusted domains during build or install processes. Enforce allow-lists for internal package sources and implement namespace validation to prevent dependency confusion.
